chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, it is said that sustenance is not brought down by anything like taʿqīb in the time between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun.”
So he said: “Yes, but I will inform you of something better than that: taking the mustache and trimming the nails on Friday.”

key_terms.التَّعْقِيبِ: post-salat supplication and devotional acts performed after prayer
key_terms.الرِّزْقُ: sustenance or provision bestowed by Allah
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, the end of the mentioned devotional time
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rising of dawn, marking the start of the early morning period
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day singled out for this practice

ai.seo_question: What deed is described as better than taʿqīb after dawn for increasing sustenance?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that taʿqīb between dawn and sunrise is known as a means for the descent of sustenance. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms this and then points to Friday grooming practices, specifically trimming the mustache and nails, as an even better act in this regard.
